Scientific Journal of School Sport, Physical Education and Psychomotricity (Sportis Sci J) es una revista de ámbito internacional y periodicidad trimestral, indexada en las principales bases de datos internacionales. Tiene como objetivo la publicación y difusión de artículos de investigación relacionados con la educación física, el deporte escolar y la psicomotricidad en niños, jóvenes y adultos. La revista admite trabajos en español e inglés desarrollados en el terreno de la investigación analítica (revisiones teóricas, de historia o síntesis), la investigación cuantitativa, la investigación experimental y/o la investigación cualitativa. Todos los manuscritos se someten a un proceso de evaluación por pares de doble ciego. text_snippet: Development of fundamental movement skills research in last decade: a systematic review and bibliometric analysis Desarrollo de la investigación sobre habilidades fundamentales del movimiento en la última década: una revisión sistemática y análisis bibliométrico This study presents a systematic review and bibliometric analysis of fundamental movement skills (FMS) research over the past decade (2015–2024), explicitly following PRISMA guidelines and utilizing VOSviewer (version 1.6.19) for bibliometric mapping. A total of 611 articles were retrieved from the Scopus database, of which 520 met the inclusion criteria after screening for peer-reviewed English articles with full-text access. The analysis reveals that FMS publications peaked in 2021 (72 articles), yet average citations per article declined sharply from 44.59 in 2015 to 2.27 in 2024. Australia contributed the highest number of publications (127; average citations 29.20), followed by the United Kingdom (103; 17.53) and the United States (62; 28.17), indicating an Anglo-centric dominance in the field. Medicine (338 publications) and Health Professions (197 publications) emerged as the dominant subject areas. It can deplete employees’ psychological resources and weaken their organizational commitment, which may lead to an increase in quiet quitting. This study examined the levels of workplace bullying, organizational commitment, and quiet quitting among sports education employees. The research is framed within Self-Determination Theory, which emphasizes the role of autonomy, competence, and relatedness in motivation and learning. Data were collected using a set of open-ended questions as the primary data collection tool. A total of 76 university students (56 males and 20 females, aged 18 to 23 years) participated in the study. Results suggest that the Attitudinal Style model, through its emphasis on autonomy support and the promotion of self-regulated learning, may enhance students' Basic Psychological Needs, fostering a more inclusive and motivating educational environment

Disruptions in this integration may restrict participation in physical activity and adversely affect quality of life. The purpose of this study was to evaluate gross motor coordination in children aged 8-9 years and to examine potential gender-related differences in motor performance. A total of 145 children (74 boys and 71 girls) from public primary schools in the urban area of Shkodra, Albania, participated in the study. Gross motor coordination was assessed using the Körperkoordinationstest für Kinder (KTK), which includes the Backward Walking, Hopping for Height (Right and Left leg), Lateral Jumps, and Platform Shifting. Descriptive and inferential statistical analyses were conducted. This qualitative systematic review and thematic synthesis examined stakeholders’ perspectives on policy implementation in SDPs across diverse international contexts. This study evaluated its implementation in university physical education using an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design. In the quantitative phase, 60 students from a state university in Davao Oriental, Philippines, were selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using the researcher-developed FunEBall Student Feedback Survey and analyzed using descriptive statistics, independent-samples t-tests, ANOVA, Tukey's HSD test, supplementary nonparametric analyses (Mann–Whitney U and Kruskal–Wallis H tests), effect size measures, and Cronbach's alpha. In the qualitative phase, open-ended responses were analyzed using thematic analysis. Results indicated that students reported very positive perceptions of FunEBall across the dimensions of engagement and participation, learning outcomes, physical activity and fitness, and enjoyment and perception. This qualitative research, framed within the interpretive paradigm, analyzed the experiences of five athletes from the Biobío Region (Chile) through semi-structured interviews and thematic analysis. The results show that the practice of Goalball operates as a meaningful occupation that transforms limiting beliefs —moving from discouragement to autonomy and self-efficacy—, promotes values such as empathy, respect, cooperation, and resilience, and channels spiritual dimensions linked to life purpose and mental strength. Furthermore, the sport contributes to the construction of a positive occupational identity, acting as a mirror of personal and collective growth. Gaps in the funding of adapted sport in Chile: the case of a public fund Despite regulatory progress in the field of inclusion, Adapted Sport remains one of the most underfunded areas within state financing. This study aims to analyze the distribution of public resources allocated to Adapted Sport in the Biobío Region of Chile, through the analysis of a regional competitive sports fund during the period 2015–2023. A quantitative, descriptive, and documentary approach was applied, with a non-experimental, longitudinal, and retrospective design. title: La danza y sus efectos sobre la coordinación motriz en escolares de educación secundaria Dance and its effects on motor coordination in secondary school students
text_snippet: La danza y sus efectos sobre la coordinación motriz en escolares de educación secundaria Dance and its effects on motor coordination in secondary school students Motor coordination is an essential component of physical and cognitive development in adolescence, with implications for academic performance, health, and social participation. Dance is proposed as a strategy to enhance these abilities in the school setting. The objective of this study was to implement a dance program with secondary school students and analyze its effects on motor coordination. A quasi-experimental design was used with 75 eighth-grade students, divided into an experimental group and a control group. The intervention consisted of 18 sessions, assessed using the Complex Motor Test. The results showed significant improvements in the experimental group, with moderate effects, explaining up to 13% of the variance. These improvements were consistent in both sexes, although males maintained an advantage in motor coordination, reflecting differences associated with social and practice factors rather than innate conditions. In conclusion, dance is an effective strategy for strengthening motor coordination in adolescents and should be systematically integrated into school physical education.
